newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says navy exercises with Israel no threat.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says navy exercises with Israel no threat.

text.p: Turkey said on Wednesday that joint naval exercises it plans to hold soon with Israel and the United States in the eastern Mediterranean do not pose a threat to neighbouring countries.

"We have said many times that this type of cooperation is being carried out without targeting any country in the region. We think it would be useful to underline this again," foreign ministry spokesman Sermet Atacanli told a news briefing.

Iran and much of the Arab world have expressed unease at Turkey's growing defence ties with the Jewish state. A deal signed last year has allowed Israeli air force jets to train in the ample air space of Turkey, a Moslem but secular country.
Atacanli said the exercises would be carried out some time in the summer. "The manoeuvres do not actually have any strategic purpose. They will be focused on search and rescue," he said.
Turkey's powerful military has overridden Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's objections to closer cooperation with Israel.
